translationRepairs: The condolence envoys Yelü Ning and his deputies ascended the hall and presented their documents; Sanyin and his party were granted court robes, caps and belts, vessels, silks, and saddled horses, while accompanying relic guardians, military officers, and others received graded gifts of clothing, silver belts, vessels, and silks.

The condolence envoys Yelü Ning and his deputies ascended the hall and presented their documents; Sanyin and his party were granted court robes, caps and belts, vessels, silks, and saddled horses, while accompanying sheli attendants, military officers, and others received graded gifts of clothing, silver belts, vessels, and silks.
舍利 here is the Khitan sheli attendant rank, not relic guardians.

Soon afterward the Sagely and Fierce Grand Empress Dowager Xuanren died; the Ministry of Rites, Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Gate Department jointly determined the protocol: if Koryŏ condolence envoys arrived around the time of the lesser auspicious rite, they were to be received at the Gate of the Hall of Purple Brightness; the Reception Office would receive their memorial and present it; they would be granted vessels, wine, and food and withdraw—all in ordinary dress with black belts, without wearing the fish tally.

Soon afterward Grand Empress Dowager Xuanren Shenglie died; the Ministry of Rites, Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Gate Department jointly determined the protocol: if Koryŏ condolence envoys arrived around the time of the lesser auspicious rite, they were to be received at the Gate of the Hall of Purple Brightness; the Reception Office would receive their memorial and present it; they would be granted vessels, wine, and food and withdraw—all in ordinary dress with black belts, without wearing the fish tally.
宣仁聖烈 is her posthumous title, not descriptive adjectives.

In the fourth month of the fifth year of Qingli (1045), the Board of Rites reported: "Pursuant to the memorial of Fiscal Commissioner Zeng Gongliang, Chief of the Board of Rites: 'When the court observes the ritual of suspending audiences upon a death, audiences should be suspended starting the day after word of bereavement arrives; those days should count toward the prescribed total, and this should be established as permanent precedent.

In the fourth month of the fifth year of Qingli (1045), the Board of Rites reported: "Pursuant to the memorial of Vice Director of Revenue and Collator of the Jixian Academy Zeng Gongliang, Administrator of the Ritual Academy: 'When the court observes the ritual of suspending audiences upon a death, audiences should be suspended starting the day after word of bereavement arrives; those days should count toward the prescribed total, and this should be established as permanent precedent.
度支員外郎、集賢校理知院 are Vice Director of Revenue, Collator of the Jixian Academy, and Administrator of the Ritual Academy.

In the first year of Jingde (1004), Li Hong died. The Board of Rites reported: "Although the rank for proclaiming lamentation is recorded in the ritual canon, in our dynasty only Zhao Pu and Cao Bin have performed this rite; we now hope Your Majesty will decide by grace."

In the first year of Jingde (1004), Li Hang died. The Board of Rites reported: "Although the rank for proclaiming lamentation is recorded in the ritual canon, in our dynasty only Zhao Pu and Cao Bin have performed this rite; we now hope Your Majesty will decide by grace."
李沆 is read Li Hang.
In the second year of Kangding, the two-year-old Imperial Prince Shouguo, Duke Xin, died. The Board of Rites held that because he had already received a title, he should be treated as an adult."
In the second year of Kangding, the two-year-old imperial son Xin, Duke of Shouguo, died. The Board of Rites held that because he had already received a title, he should be treated as an adult."
壽國公昕: Xin, Duke of Shouguo.

In the fifth month of the second year of Shaoxing (1132), Vice Director of Personnel Li Guang had ruled that persons who died within thirty days of a bone fracture from a fall sustained more than fifty days earlier qualified for the prescribed silver grant.

In the fifth month of the second year of Shaoxing (1132), Vice Minister of Personnel Li Guang had ruled that persons who died within thirty days of a bone fracture from a fall sustained more than fifty days earlier qualified for the prescribed silver grant.
吏部侍郎 is Vice Minister of Personnel.

At this time Vice Director of Revenue Song Kuang reported: "Since that time limit was established, most claims have involved persons who died of unrelated illnesses; descendants schemed for the reward, colluded with local officials, fabricated nominal assignments, and submitted fraudulent petitions—a clear abuse."

At this time Vice Minister of Revenue Song Kuang reported: "Since that time limit was established, most claims have involved persons who died of unrelated illnesses; descendants schemed for the reward, colluded with local officials, fabricated nominal assignments, and submitted fraudulent petitions—a clear abuse."
戶部侍郎 is Vice Minister of Revenue.

One jade tablet and two bolts of hsien silk were to be granted, along with a young-ox sacrificial feast; the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Court of the Imperial Treasury, and Directorate of the Palace Domestic Service were requested to supply these according to ritual.

One jade tablet and two bolts of hsien silk were to be granted, along with the shaolao (sheep-and-pig) sacrificial offering; the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Court of the Imperial Treasury, and Directorate of the Palace Domestic Service were requested to supply these according to ritual.
少牢 is the sheep-and-pig offering, not an ox.

Circuit enfeoffment: in the first year of Jianlong (960), the late Gao Baorong, specially advanced and King of Nanping, was posthumously granted Grand Marshal by imperial order; in the first year of Duan Gong (988), the late Qian Shu, Grand Preceptor and King of Deng, was specially posthumously enfeoffed as King of Qin—that is the precedent.

Circuit enfeoffment: in the first year of Jianlong (960), the late Gao Baorong, specially advanced and King of Nanping, was posthumously granted Grand Marshal by imperial order; in the first year of Duan Gong (988), the late Qian Chu, Grand Preceptor and King of Deng, was specially posthumously enfeoffed as King of Qin—that is the precedent.
錢俶 is read Qian Chu.
Later, Hanlin Compiler Hu Dan observed: "Under the old system, civil and military officials received posthumous title canons according to their merit and conduct.
Later, Auxiliary of the Historiography Institute Hu Dan observed: "Under the old system, civil and military officials received posthumous title canons according to their merit and conduct.
直史館 is Auxiliary of the Historiography Institute.
Wang Hao, Academician of the Hall for Veneration of Excellence, argued: "A posthumous title is the outward expression of a person's conduct.
Wang Hao, Auxiliary of the Jixian Academy, argued: "A posthumous title is the outward expression of a person's conduct.
直集賢院 is Auxiliary of the Jixian Academy.
Only when Duke Wei Gongsun Wenzi died did his son Shu request a posthumous title.
